transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Honestly, I'm really embarrassed to even talk about this, but when I get stressed after work and classes, I end up eating way more food in one sitting than seems normal for anyone. It's just gotten to the point where I feel like I really need some help.
When you eat large amounts of food, do you feel like you’ve lost control during those episodes, and do they happen regularly—like at least once a week for several weeks?

Yes, completely. Once I start, it feels like I'm on autopilot and I just can't stop myself, even when I'm telling myself to put the food down. This has been happening at least once a week, sometimes more, for about four months now since my workload and classes got so overwhelming.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["F50.5", "F50.0"], but based on this conversation, F50.0 (Anorexia nervosa) seems unlikely because there is no indication of restrictive eating, fear of weight gain, or body image disturbance. Instead, the patient describes recurrent episodes of binge eating with a sense of loss of control occurring at least once a week for several months, which strongly supports F50.5 (Binge eating disorder). No other differential diagnoses currently fit as well.
